Subject: Capacity MAP & close checklist — draft (Novus Health)

Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a draft mutual action plan (MAP) that ties the evaluation gates to a phased capacity reservation and close timeline. High-level summary up front so your procurement and engineering teams can scan quickly: 

- Evaluation window: 3 weeks (pilot + perf gates) — target start: Jun 21, 2027.
- Acceptance criteria: throughput >= 12K TPS-equivalent across 2 prompt classes; end-to-end 95th pct latency < 220ms for interactive scenarios; quality regression delta <= 2% vs baseline prompts.
- Initial committed pool: 4 x H100 (reserved capacity) for 90 days following signature; scale path to 12–16 x H100 within 90–120 days after baseline acceptance depending on traffic.
- Staggered tranche option: sign for 4x now, add 4x at +45 days, final 4–8x at +90 days.
- Lead time note: Dedicated/private deployments on H100 typically have provisioning lead times of 6–8 weeks once the contract is executed and network prerequisites are complete. On-prem options vary by customer infra.
- Acceptance handoff: We’ll run a two-week canary in your dev VPC (if private) or our dedicated tenant (if hosted) before switching traffic.

Requested next steps: please review attached MAP (MAP-NovusHealth-v2.xlsx) and GPU-sizing doc, confirm whether you prefer the staggered tranche, and flag any internal procurement checkpoints (finance approval, SOC 2 evidences, PO template). If you can commit to an internal signature target by 2027-06-30 we can lock current SKU/lead times.

I’ll follow up early next week with a proposed SOW draft and DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Appreciate the clear summary and the MAP doc. A few quick clarifying questions from the procurement and infra sides: 

1) Lead times — you mention 6–8 weeks post-signature. If we do a staggered tranche, can the second tranche be queued earlier so we don’t face a fresh 6–8 week wait?
2) SOC 2 and evidence — our security team needs SOC 2 Type II evidence plus a list of where logs/audit trails are retained. Can you point us to the relevant artifacts or a contact?
3) Pricing — procurement is asking whether we can move the initial commit to 3 months with an automatic renewal unless we downgrade. Also asking about a short-term credit if we need to extend the pilot.

We’re targeting an internal procurement decision by the end of June but I want to surface these items now. I’ve CC’d procurement for visibility.

Elena / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick read. Responses inline below and an updated plan attached (SOW-draft.docx + GPU-sizing-v2.pdf with explicit SKU/lead-time table).

1) Lead times & queuing: yes — we can queue tranche 2 provisioning as a queued reservation provided signatures and a purchase order are in place. Practically this means you sign the master agreement and issue a PO for tranche 1 + queued request for tranche 2. Provisioning for tranche 2 then proceeds as soon as we reach the scheduled date; we guarantee the earlier quoted lead time if the queued PO is present.

2) SOC 2 artifacts: our security team will share a secure link to the SOC 2 Type II report and our audit-log retention policy. I’ll introduce you to our security contact (karthik.iyer@redwood.ai) — he’s copied on the internal note below.

3) Pricing / credit: We can offer a 30-day evaluation credit applied to the initial tranche for pilot usage (not cumulative with other promos). For the contract term we can accept a 3-month initial commit with automatic monthly renewal unless Novus notifies cancellation 30 days prior to renewal.

Operational notes:
- Canary plan: week 0–2 smoke + perf tests in dev tenant; week 2–4 gradual ramp to 10–15% traffic; week 5 cutover if gates pass.
- Acceptance owner: Novus engineering signs off on perf gates; Redwood will provide test harness and baseline prompt set.
- Escalations: if perf regressions are detected, we’ll revert traffic to prior model and do a joint RCA within 48 hours.

If procurement confirms the queued-tranche PO flow and SOC 2 link is acceptable, we’ll prepare a final SOW and DocuSign envelope targeted at Jun 28–30. Attaching SOW-draft.docx and GPU-sizing-v2.pdf.

Best,
Laura

Team —

Forwarding the Novus thread. Procurement is pushing hard on a 3-month initial commit and wants SOC 2 artifacts. They indicated end-of-June signature target. A few suggested positions before I respond: 

- Offer: 30-day pilot credit (already committed above) + 7% list discount if they sign by 2027-06-30 (time-limited).
- Tranche mechanics: accept queued PO model but require a non-refundable commitment deposit for tranche 2 (equivalent to first 30 days of tranche 2) to secure capacity queue. This buys us protection vs last-minute drop-offs.
- SLA ask: require that Novus engages security review within 10 business days of receiving SOC 2 link; if not, we push provisioning by 2 weeks to protect other queued customers.

Notes on sizing: GPU-sizing-v2 assumes 4x H100 equates to ~45M tokens/min for our benchmark prompt mix; scale to 12x to handle initial production peaks. If procurement wants to keep cost down, steer them to a spike-bursting approach with our Dedicated + burst in hosted.

Please advise if we should escalate pricing authority to sales ops for a higher discount (10–12%) if they ask. I’ll hold off on final SOW until we confirm the queued PO + deposit language.

Thanks,
Laura
